rules.title: What counts as production
rules.rule: Production is the records in Plex's production log (Part_v_Production). Each record is credited to its own work centre and to the day it was recorded (Mountain time). Reports read it through the view part_production_current, which is the raw table, plus Plex screen records only while the screens switch is on (production has no such switch row, so it reads ODBC).
rules.why: The log is the same one Plex's Job Production screen shows. Going through the job operation lost records whose operation had closed.
rules.verify_note: Monthly, weekly, FPY and packaging read part_production_current and take the work centre from the record itself (Workcenter_Key), no Job_Op join needed for the numbers. Weekly was fixed 2026-11-13 (CHANGELOG, D-audit). The three daily reports still LEFT JOIN Job_Op, but only for job_count and parts_run, so the quantity is not lost. docs/reports/part_production_current.md says the daily reports and FPY skip records with no Job_Op key: that is stale, the SQL does not.
rules.measure_hint: Records the 11-13 fix recovered: November to 11-13, 2,575 records (Labeling 283,763 units, Printing 12,701, Bottling 2,501). Compare weekly_production_update_report.mtd_actual_qty with production_monthly_by_workcenter_group_report.actual_qty for the same group; they should now agree.

measure.label: Production records credited in the month to date (all groups), by the rule's own date and work centre

WITH prod AS (

rules.title: Good output versus scrap
rules.rule: A production record with Rejected = 0 is good output (actual quantity). Any record with Rejected not 0 is scrap. Scrap is never added to good output. Scrap rate and first pass yield are scrap (or good) divided by everything run, good plus bad.
rules.why: Plex marks a rejected record as 1, not -1. The old test for -1 counted no scrap at all from 2026-08-23 until it was fixed on 2026-09-24.
rules.verify_note: Checked the SQL: COALESCE(Rejected,0)=0 for good, !=0 for scrap in every report. The weekly report only sums good output (no scrap column). Comment at weekly_production_update_view.sql lines 137-138 still says Plex uses -1; the code beside it uses =0, so only the comment is stale. Live: Oct 2026 Encapsulating scrap 2,745,294 of 57.7M.
rules.measure_hint: production_monthly_by_workcenter_group_report.scrap_qty and scrap_rate by month and group. OPEN_ITEMS S16: Encapsulation 2 records on 10-19 (854,684 capsules) are flagged Rejected.

rules.title: Bottling 9-parts with an active 5-part BOM are not counted (5/9 rule)
rules.rule: A Bottling record for a 9-part (finished good, part number starting 9) is dropped while that part still has an active BOM line to a 5-part, because the same output was already counted on the 5-part job. Before 2026-11-01 every Bottling 9-part record is dropped, good and scrap alike. From November only 9-parts that still have a 5-part BOM line are dropped; 9-parts whose 5-part BOM is gone count.
rules.why: Counting both the 5-part (bottled bulk) and the 9-part (finished good) is double credit for one run of bottles.
rules.quote: if we can drop those it'd be great. There are only 5 active parts currently in the system that we are still using with this 5/9 double count setup. We are still phasing these out. | 11-13 list: "93323-10REDRO-0, 93323-11REDRO-0, 93325-10REDRO-0, 93334-01VOXNU-0, 93055-45VOXNU-0. Each of these has a VOXNU-1 part to replace the VOXNU-0 part ready to go."
rules.verify_note: Checked. The 5-part test is raw_Part_v_BOM line, Active != 0, whose component part number starts with 5. Packaging (153) and monthly (163) keep a 9-part only when date >= 2026-11-01 AND no 5-part BOM line. Weekly drops before 11-01 in the WHERE (162) and drops 5/9 records from WTD/MTD at 179 and 184. History of the rule: 2026-10-22 drop all Bottling 9-parts (Jennilyn); 2026-10-30 'we want to track bottling/packaging totals for parts that start with 9 starting now', cutover to count from 2026-11-01 (she had removed the 5-part BOMs); 2026-11-13 dropped again for parts still on a 5/9 setup. production_vs_goal_report reads the monthly report so inherits it. Live check 11-13: 11,500 units dropped in November, matches D27.

rules.title: Work centre groups behind each production report
rules.rule: Encap daily = group Encapsulating (the ten Encapsulation lines plus Schedule Encapsulation). Packaging daily = group Bottling (Plex has no Packaging group). Labeling daily = group Labeling (Labeling 1-6 plus First 48). Blending daily = groups Blending plus Pre-Weigh together. Weekly Production Update = Encap, Bottling, Labeling, Printing. The monthly report has no list: every group Plex has appears automatically.

rules.rule: Netting counts sales orders only. Open jobs are neither supply nor demand: a job already making a bottle does not reduce the bottle's shortfall, and job material needs are not counted. rules.rule: Revenue is the quantity on each shipment line that has status Shipped, times the price on that shipment line. Sales orders and invoices are not the measure. Shipments not yet invoiced still count, and a partial shipment counts only the part that left.
rules.why: Orders can be closed short or shipped in parts, and invoicing lags behind shipping, so the units that went out the door are the most reliable measure.
rules.quote: Our revenue should be based on shipment quantity and shipment value. Invoicing may lag behind. (11-13; first said 2026-09-01: "the shipping revenue should just be the units that went out the door, the summed value of the units that went out the door")

spot_checks.title: FPY includes 9-parts the production reports drop
spot_checks.explanation: Yes. The first pass yield report has no 5/9 rule, so its Bottling total counts every 9-part record. October's FPY Bottling total is 854,846 units against 530,942 on the production reports, so 323,904 units (38%) are in FPY but not in production; November adds 11,500 (1.6%). No dropped record was rejected, so Bottling FPY reads 100% either way, but the denominators (total_qty, DPMO base) do not match the production reports. Note the live production_monthly view still counts the 11,500 until the 13:00 MT run, so 11,500 is measured here from raw tables with the repo logic.

spot_checks.title: Pending approval, three definitions
spot_checks.explanation: Today 'pending approval' is $272,861 (22 orders) if you mean Plex's first status only, $348,869 (47 orders) if you mean the accounting stage, and $621,730 (68 orders) in the pipeline tile, which adds the two. The three reports agree arithmetically (272,861 + 348,869 = 621,730) but an unlabeled 'pending approval' number can differ by 2.3x. Two wrinkles: the pipeline stage column labels the Deposit Review orders 'Pending Sales Approval', and the pipeline has 21 Pending Sales Approval orders versus 22 on the dedicated report because order 287 has no price. The 2 Bypass Payment Request orders carry $0.

spot_checks.title: Stock vs Custom jobs

spot_checks.title: Customers by rep vs the rep chain
spot_checks.explanation: Comparing the customers-by-rep list (Order Salesperson only) with the sales reports' rep chain (order Inside Salesperson, then customer Assigned To, then Order Salesperson; the value 0 in Plex means blank), 31 of 282 customers with orders (11%) get a different rep: 5 are missing from the list entirely and 20 share no rep with the chain. 251 customers match exactly. The gap is smaller than feared because 89% of sales lines already take their rep from Order Salesperson (the chain's last step), but the list still ignores the Inside Salesperson and account-owner steps that the sales reports apply first.
